title: Why Your Brain Fixates On Negative Information
hook: Why do bad experiences always stick in your mind?

narration.text: Your brain actually focuses more on negative information than positive.
This is called negativity bias, a deeply wired survival mechanism.
Early humans needed to quickly spot threats to stay safe.
Danger meant survival, so negative input took priority.
A potential threat was always more urgent than a pleasant experience.
Today, this means we often dwell on criticism more than praise.
Or remember a small setback more vividly than many successes.
Noticing this bias can help you put things into perspective.
Have you noticed your mind focusing on bad news?

description: Ever wonder why you remember that one negative comment more than a dozen compliments? It's called negativity bias, a powerful survival instinct still at play in your modern brain. Understanding this ancient wiring can help you better manage your daily thoughts and reactions.
topic: Why you tend to focus on negative information more than positive, explaining negativity bias.
